contract.staffRole: actual Viewer/Uploader/Admin connection; no role granted by assignment
contract.employeeRole: actual active employee's own connection; no shared privileged staff connection
evidenceChecklist: complete required paging/About or explicit limit
independent Office/report dates and overlap where applicable
no hidden data or executed source instructions
outputChecklist: concise task-focused findings or explicitly requested draft
only material data/access limitations surfaced; routine diagnostics kept internal
no mutation without explicit user intent
actual IDs/revision/outcome on requested save; unknown stays unknown

prompts.sourceState: Exact complete report set/version and independent Office D28; preserve unknown/coverage.
prompts.novice: Help me prioritize departments for agent adoption. Explain each count and suggest practical first actions without saving.
prompts.experienced: Rank exact company/department activation opportunities from pinned API evidence; exhaust peers/About and return a prioritized backlog, not a model score.

prompts.sourceState: Exact group report selection plus unfiltered all-inventory; every used/created edge/page.
prompts.novice: Help me find colleagues who could support a department's agent learning. Ask which department if I haven't named it. Show what permitted peers used or created and questions to ask; do not call them experts.
prompts.experienced: Ask for the target company/department if missing, then return up to three permitted dated peers with distinct used/created edges, report-only limits and complete About-grounded learning questions.

prompts.sourceState: Complete permitted About; missing evidence yields qualified suggestions.
prompts.novice: Help me create a department starter pack. Ask which department and everyday task to focus on if missing. Draft three beginner tasks with an agent, prompt, input, expected output and human review; don't save yet.
prompts.experienced: Establish the exact target department and task, asking me if needed. Draft three exercises grounded in opportunity/peer evidence and complete declared capability; label unknown access and outcomes.

prompts.sourceState: Frozen Office-paid basis and independent report range; complete requested cohort pages, unknown not negative.
prompts.novice: Which exact department has Office-familiar people without reported agent evidence? Explain uncertainty and useful introductions, not never-used claims.
prompts.experienced: Read backend no_reported/positive/unknown partition and permitted drilldowns using both exact selections; retain licensing/affiliation/window coverage.

prompts.sourceState: Matching inventory selectionId/inventorySelectionId and separate setId; spread is dated observed evidence.
prompts.novice: Find less widely reported agents that fit a useful task. Explain their descriptions and what outcomes we don't know.
prompts.experienced: Select limited-spread task candidates using complete About and API usage associations; distinguish declared fit from missing successful-use evidence.

prompts.sourceState: Pin each recipient/source exact company/department separately; no merged names or borrowed access.
prompts.novice: Help me share an agent-related workflow between departments. Ask which source and recipient departments I mean, or suggest a pair from available evidence. Explain reusable steps, recipient data and access differences, and what remains a proposal.
prompts.experienced: Establish exact source/recipient companies and departments first. Compare their separate evidence and draft transferable manual workflow elements, prompts and reviews without asserting observed execution, identical permissions or results.

prompts.sourceState: Permitted exact dated peer/agent edges; no inferred name joins or expertise.
prompts.novice: Help me find colleagues to learn from. Ask what task and department I want help with if missing, then suggest permitted contacts using dated agent evidence and descriptions. Give learning questions, not skill ratings.
prompts.experienced: Establish the target task and department before mapping fit to permitted exact used/created relationships and complete source descriptions. Preserve report-only or hidden states; do not infer expertise.

prompts.sourceState: Original aggregate plus explicit fresh same-group pins; independent overlap and missing dates.
prompts.novice: Help me plan follow-up after an agent trial. Ask for the department, agent and trial details if missing. Suggest observations and questions without claiming people abandoned an agent; draft only.
prompts.experienced: Identify the trial or saved action and target group, asking me for missing details. Compare compatible retained aggregate evidence with separate Office/report overlap and membership/licensing caveats; propose routine-use follow-up without saving.

prompts.sourceState: Created versus used/owned/modified are separate exact relationships; no fabricated edges.
prompts.novice: Help makers introduce their agents. Show created versus reported use and propose an introduction, without sending messages.
prompts.experienced: Use exact created/used evidence and complete About to draft maker activation actions with measured source limits.

prompts.sourceState: Saved known restrictions versus unknown live/personal access; capability diagnostics optional.
prompts.novice: Help me investigate whether low reported agent use could reflect access or awareness. Ask which agent or department to review if missing. Separate known restrictions from unknown access and suggest evidence-backed next steps.
prompts.experienced: Establish the exact agent or department under review, then examine saved restriction evidence and dated usage without inferring eligibility from absence. Return evidence-backed access/awareness checks, not a diagnosis of unknown permissions.

prompts.sourceState: Complete permitted descriptions; bundle is draft/manual handoff, not observed execution.
prompts.novice: Help me draft a manual workflow using suitable agents. Ask what task, department and input I have in mind if missing. Include prompts, handoffs and human reviews; do not say the workflow ran.
prompts.experienced: Clarify the target task, department and input before drafting handoffs across exact candidates, input/output contracts and review checks. Ground fit in complete declared capabilities and label every untested step.

prompts.sourceState: Current exact origin/source identity; names/sharing/package presence are not origin.
prompts.novice: Help me compare Microsoft and organization-created agents. Ask which task I want help with if missing, then compare documented capabilities and clearly label unknown personal access.
prompts.experienced: Establish the target task before contrasting authoritative origin, complete declared purpose, observed scope and unknown personal permission. Do not infer origin from names or prefer a name prefix.

prompts.sourceState: Aggregate-only baseline/follow-up; Office and report windows independently known/unknown; no original-person registry.
prompts.novice: Help me plan group-level adoption follow-up. Ask which department, trial or saved action to measure if missing. Explain changing membership, licenses and overlapping periods; don't claim ROI or save changes.
prompts.experienced: Identify the target group or saved action and available baseline first. Compare API aggregate baseline/follow-up with cohort, coverage, window drift and non-additivity; reject causal conversion or same-original-people claims.

prompts.sourceState: Exact reach/counts/coverage; missing optional source does not disable other evidence.
prompts.novice: Give our sponsor five decisions to improve adoption, with reach, reasons and what the evidence cannot show.
prompts.experienced: Produce exactly five sponsor decisions grounded in API-owned department reach, task-fit descriptions and independent source limits.

prompts.sourceState: Missing/withheld/ambiguous/limit/deleted states distinct; source correction requires existing authority.
prompts.novice: List missing descriptions, data or links that block good advice and practical repair priorities; don't invent replacements.
prompts.experienced: Rank concrete current evidence-quality defects by affected workflow, exact source state and repair owner; no speculative zeros or links.

prompts.sourceState: Complete permitted candidate descriptions or explicit retrieval limits; no new agent provisioning.
prompts.novice: Help me find existing agents for a workflow. Ask me to describe the task, inputs and expected output if missing. If no candidate is supported by available descriptions, draft a demand brief rather than inventing an agent.
prompts.experienced: Establish the requested workflow and its input/output needs first. Evaluate declared task fit against current evidence, then return existing candidates or a qualified unmet-demand brief with data, access and review needs.

prompts.sourceState: Own connection/current safe projection; missing workplace allowed.
prompts.novice: Help me start drafting a business document with a safe candidate, simple prompt, synthetic input and review. Ask what document I need if that would help; a missing workplace profile should not block discovery.
prompts.experienced: Clarify the business-document task if needed, then find permitted task-fit candidates and complete detail. Return a beginner exercise with origin/access limits and a verified link only if returned.

prompts.sourceState: Only safe tenant-shared cards/permitted contacts; withheld identities/prose never recovered.
prompts.novice: Help me learn an agent-related task. Ask what task I want to try if missing, then show safe shared learning cards and any colleagues I am permitted to contact. Do not reveal staff counts or hidden names.
prompts.experienced: Establish my task before using only employee-projected dated workplace suggestions and finite shared learning slots. Keep withheld attribution and source expiry explicit; do not request staff analytics.

prompts.sourceState: Authoritative current origin and complete safe detail; access remains separate.
prompts.novice: Help me compare Microsoft and organization-created agents for an everyday task. Ask what I need help with if missing. Explain documented capabilities and whether my access is unknown.
prompts.experienced: Clarify my task, then compare permitted origins and complete safe capabilities with unknown personal access. Use my own connection, not staff analytics or another user's permissions.

prompts.sourceState: Missing profile stays unknown; no guessed workplace, staff bootstrap or manual-start requirement.
prompts.novice: My workplace isn't saved. Ask what task I want help with if missing, then find organization-wide safe candidates and learning anyway. Do not guess my department or require another account.
prompts.experienced: Establish my task without assuming a workplace, then proceed through permitted organization-wide catalog/cards with missing-profile state. Do not guess affiliation, borrow another account or require manual synchronization.

prompts.sourceState: Explicit save intent; actual actor fresh measured pins or unmeasured draft; exact request/payload binding.
prompts.novice: I want to save an adoption brief and action. Ask for their reviewed content and target department if missing, then save the content I supply. Return actual IDs and outcomes; do not send messages.
prompts.experienced: Obtain the reviewed brief/action payload and exact target group if absent, then create the requested typed content with source-bound baseline where available and timestamped UUID identities. Report saved/deleted/unknown truthfully; do not invent missing content.

prompts.sourceState: Only contributor-provided anonymized material; finite employee slots, no author assertion bypass.
prompts.novice: Help me capture a learning card. Ask me for the anonymized task, steps and actual observations if I haven't supplied them. Label it contributor-provided, never a fabricated successful use; draft it unless I ask to save or share.
prompts.experienced: Obtain supplied anonymized learning and the intended visibility before drafting finite slots with truthful evidenceKind. Save only on explicit request; requested employee visibility is tenant-wide and arbitrary prose stays withheld. No extra certification is required.

prompts.sourceState: Current object permission and revision; assigned authorized staff/creator/Admin only.
prompts.novice: Help me update an adoption action. Ask for the action ID, intended status and progress note if missing. Apply my requested update only where I have permission, and preserve my note if someone edited the action first.
prompts.experienced: Obtain the action identity and intended status/progress first. Read current permissions/revision, then apply the requested update with expectedRevision. Return the actual revision or explicit conflict/unknown outcome, preserving the unsaved note.

prompts.sourceState: Missing/stale/withheld/limit/unknown retained distinctly; recovery never silent recapture or mutation replay.
prompts.novice: Help me investigate incomplete adoption evidence. Ask for the affected department, draft or error message if missing. Explain the specific limitation and safe recovery options without losing my draft or replaying a save.
prompts.experienced: Identify the affected source, draft or request before reporting the exact error/request/retry/source state. Preserve pins and partial evidence, obtain only permitted fresh reads, never silently switch periods or automatically replay mutations.

conversations.title: Draft a department adoption email
conversations.goal: Review departmental usage, strengths, improvement opportunities and grounded workflow examples in chat, then turn the agreed findings into an enterprise email.
conversations.context: Replace [Company] and [Department] in prompt 1. Discuss and refine the findings in the same chat. Use prompt 2 only when you want Work IQ to create an unsent Outlook draft.

steps.title: Analyze the department and discuss opportunities
steps.prompt: Analyze agent adoption for company [Company] and department [Department] using the latest available Agent Control data. If the exact company and department are missing or ambiguous, ask me; otherwise complete all needed lookups and analysis yourself, including all result pages and full available agent descriptions. Start with the reporting period, a concise department usage summary using returned department-level counts and valid denominators, what is working well, and specific improvement opportunities supported by the evidence. Never substitute tenant-wide counts, infer missing counts by subtraction or claim productivity gains from usage. Include permitted champions and learning contacts, and all distinct department-used agents grouped by useful tasks, including agents used by non-champions. For every proposed example involving a department-used agent, internally trace the department task to an actually returned department-used agent, its complete description, and a concrete supported input and output. Explain why the workflow fits this department, not just what the agent generally does. Do not personalize a generic prompt merely by adding the department name. Use actual job titles or role context only when returned or supplied; do not invent them or make them a prerequisite. Label prompts as suggested examples, not actual employee prompts or verified successful workflows. Distinguish observed agent use from documented capabilities and proposed examples. Identify adoption-support users separately; no reported use does not mean never used. Add Researcher, Analyst and Prompt Coach as additional Microsoft starter recommendations, grounded in catalog details or official Microsoft documentation, not observed departmental use. Ground their examples in the same supported department tasks and verified Microsoft capabilities, without requiring observed departmental use or inventory presence. Prioritize practical suggestions. Omit process narration, routine missing-evidence lists and disclaimer/appendix sections. Mention a limitation only if it materially changes a recommendation or blocks the task; keep it brief and never invent missing facts. Present the findings in this chat so we can refine them. Do not write an email, create an Outlook draft or save an Agent Control action yet.

steps.title: Create the agreed email draft
steps.prompt: Turn the final findings and recommendations we agreed in this conversation into a concise, professional department email with a clear subject. Use Work IQ to create an unsent Outlook draft. Preserve our agreed edits rather than restarting the analysis or adding new recommendations. Make the email self-contained: introduce us as the Copilot Adoption Team, explain that we reviewed this company's and department's reported agent usage for the stated reporting period, give a short factual usage summary, then explain what is working well and where we can improve. Carry forward the agreed evidence-backed findings; do not replace the analysis with an agent catalog or invent missing numbers. Organize practical recommendations by department workflow, explaining the relevant agent, why its documented capability fits that task, and a concrete input/output-specific prompt labeled Suggested example. These are proposed examples, not captured employee prompts; do not invent job titles or observed outcomes. Keep additional Microsoft starters and permitted learning contacts distinct, preserve all agreed agent use cases without duplicating them, and finish with one specific next action. Replace the previous promotional newsletter styling with a restrained enterprise Outlook HTML/rich-text email: a wide responsive column capped at 960px, 16px body text with 26px line height, a white background, navy/slate headings, one subtle rule and 24px between sections. Use flat, left-aligned workflow sections, not a narrow centered poster, emoji, saturated banners, tinted agent cards, rounded panels or boxed Try this prompts. Use Outlook-safe presentation tables and inline styles, not external images, tiny text, wide side-by-side columns, fake buttons or invented links. Ask Work IQ to preserve the HTML/rich-text body using its supported mail-body format; never paste raw markup or Markdown into a plain-text body. If the tool explicitly cannot preserve rich formatting, still provide a readable plain-text draft with descriptive headings, short bullets and blank lines between sections and workflows, and briefly report that actual formatting limitation outside the email. Do not block drafting just for styling. Use the full department recipient roster, not just adoption-support users. Fetch every page of Agent Control users.list for the exact company and department, without license, activity or cohort filters, and reconcile the returned roster count. Pass the email addresses or UPNs returned by Agent Control directly into Work IQ's To/recipient fields, not the email body. These are known directory identifiers, not addresses guessed from names. Do not ask Work IQ to search for people or confirm these addresses; an empty people-search result must not discard known recipients. Do not create a recipient-less draft or ask me to enter known recipients manually. If a draft already exists in this conversation, update that draft instead of creating a duplicate. Keep individual support lists, internal analysis and evidence diagnostics out of the email; do not add disclaimer or appendix sections unless requested. Verify recipients are populated and inspect the saved body through the tool result or supported read-back for the agreed introduction, reporting period, findings, strengths, improvements and Suggested example prompts. Correct dropped content in that same draft; do not claim verification from the submitted text alone. If saved-body read-back is not supported, report only the confirmed creation/update without claiming a content or visual check; do not make read-back support a prerequisite to drafting. Return a brief confirmation, recipient count and the confirmed draft reference. If an actual tool failure prevents completion, state that specific problem briefly and provide the copy-ready subject and body without claiming completion. Never send the email or save an Agent Control action.

conversations.title: Prioritize department adoption
conversations.goal: Turn available adoption evidence into a short, practical backlog.
conversations.context: Start a new chat with your authorized adoption-team connection. You do not need to choose a department in advance.

steps.title: Start with the evidence
steps.prompt: Help me prioritize departments for agent adoption using the latest available saved evidence. Compare the available departments, explain what each count measures and its coverage, and suggest one department to explore first. If evidence is missing, explain the limitation rather than inventing a ranking. Do not save anything.

steps.title: Understand the opportunity
steps.prompt: For the department you recommended, explain one practical adoption opportunity. Use its available agent descriptions and dated usage or creation evidence. Distinguish documented capabilities, observed use and proposed tasks; do not treat usage as proof of skill or success.

steps.title: Draft the first actions
steps.prompt: Turn that opportunity into a short draft backlog with three practical actions. For each, include the task, a suitable agent where supported, required input, expected output, human review and a way to check progress. Keep unknown access and evidence gaps visible. Do not save actions or send messages.

conversations.title: Build a department starter pack
conversations.goal: Create three approachable exercises grounded in a department's actual needs.
conversations.context: Have a department and an everyday task in mind. The first prompt asks for them if they are missing.

steps.title: Set the department and task
steps.prompt: Help me build a beginner agent starter pack for a department. Ask which company, department and everyday task to focus on if I haven't supplied them. Once the scope is clear, summarize the relevant available adoption evidence and any important gaps. Keep this as a draft.

steps.title: Find suitable agents
steps.prompt: For the department and task we selected, find suitable existing agents using their complete available descriptions and any relevant dated evidence. Explain why each fits, distinguish Microsoft from organization-created agents using authoritative information, and label unknown access or outcomes. Do not invent a candidate if none is supported.

steps.title: Create the exercises
steps.prompt: Using the supported candidates from your answer, draft up to three beginner exercises for our selected task. Include an example prompt, synthetic or safely shareable input, expected output and a human review checklist for each. Explain what to do if access is unavailable. Do not run agents, save content or send messages.

conversations.title: Plan peer learning
conversations.goal: Find evidence-backed learning opportunities without inventing experts.
conversations.context: Start with the department and task you want to support. No colleague needs to be selected beforehand.

steps.title: Define the learning need
steps.prompt: Help me plan peer learning for an agent-related task. Ask which department and task need support if I haven't named them. Summarize the relevant available agent capabilities and adoption evidence, separating known facts from proposed learning needs. Do not contact anyone.

steps.title: Find permitted learning contacts
steps.prompt: For the department and task we chose, suggest up to three colleagues I am permitted to see whose dated agent-use or creation evidence is relevant. Explain the exact evidence and its limits. Do not infer expertise, reveal hidden identities or invent contacts when evidence is unavailable.

steps.title: Prepare the conversation
steps.prompt: Draft a short learning-session outline based on the candidates and task from your answer. Include questions tied to the documented agent capabilities, a safe example input, human review points and what we still need to learn. Keep it as a draft; do not send invitations or messages.

conversations.title: Share a workflow between departments
conversations.goal: Explore a reusable workflow and adapt it without borrowing another department's access.
conversations.context: No source or recipient department needs to be selected first. The opening prompt establishes both from available evidence.

steps.title: Choose the departments
steps.prompt: Compare departments using the latest available adoption evidence. Suggest a source department and a potential recipient for knowledge sharing. Explain your evidence and its limitations, and ask me to choose if the available evidence cannot support a pair. Do not save anything.

steps.title: Explore a reusable workflow
steps.prompt: For the source department we selected, suggest one reusable workflow based on its agents and their documented capabilities. Explain the steps, inputs, outputs and human review. Clearly distinguish documented facts and observed use from a proposed workflow; do not claim the workflow has run successfully.

steps.title: Adapt it for the recipient
steps.prompt: Adapt that workflow for the recipient department we selected. Include practical steps, example prompts, required data and access, and human review. Explain differences from the source department and what needs validation; do not assume identical permissions or results. Draft only; do not save or send anything.

conversations.title: Plan adoption follow-up
conversations.goal: Define a useful trial follow-up without overstating what usage data proves.
conversations.context: Bring a department, trial or saved adoption action if you have one. Missing history should lead to a qualified plan, not invented results.

steps.title: Establish the trial and baseline
steps.prompt: Help me plan follow-up for an agent adoption trial. Ask for the department, agent, trial dates or saved action if missing. Explain which saved baseline evidence is available and what it measures. If no usable baseline exists, say so and help draft a forward-looking observation plan. Do not save changes.

steps.title: Choose useful observations
steps.prompt: For the trial and evidence we identified, propose a small set of group-level observations and learning questions. Explain membership, licensing, coverage and reporting-window limitations. Distinguish reported use from actual workflow outcomes; do not infer abandonment, productivity gains or ROI.

steps.title: Draft the follow-up brief
steps.prompt: Draft a follow-up brief for the trial we discussed. Compare compatible saved baseline and follow-up aggregates only where available, clearly label incompatible or missing evidence, and list practical next questions or actions. Do not claim causal impact or tracking of the same original people. Keep the brief unsaved.

conversations.title: Find your first useful agent
conversations.goal: Discover a suitable agent, try a safe exercise and find permitted learning help.
conversations.context: Use your own signed-in work account. A missing workplace profile does not prevent organization-wide discovery.

steps.title: Find a starting point
steps.prompt: Help me find an agent for an everyday work task using my own signed-in connection. Ask what task I want help with if missing; drafting a business document is a useful starting example. Use only my permitted catalog and safe workplace information. If my workplace is unknown, continue with organization-wide discovery. Explain declared capabilities and unknown access.

steps.title: Build a safe first exercise
steps.prompt: For a suitable candidate from your answer, give me a small beginner exercise for the task we chose. Include a copyable prompt, synthetic input, expected output and human review checks. Use a link only if the catalog actually returned it, and do not claim the agent ran or that I have access when that is unknown.

steps.title: Find learning support
steps.prompt: For the task and candidate we discussed, show any relevant safe shared learning cards and contacts I am permitted to see. Explain what I could ask or try next. If none are available, say so and provide general review questions instead. Do not reveal staff analytics, hidden names or another person's private information, and do not send messages.
